title: The month of Asarh
hookLine: in Asarh the heat burns those who don't have the Lord near (Barah Maha, ang 134)

lines: THE SAME HEAT, NOT THE SAME FOR ALL.
cards: June into July. The fields are cracked. The canals run low.

Everyone keeps looking at the sky, waiting for the monsoon, and every day the clouds gather and don't break. People sleep on rooftops for a breath of air. The heat of Asarh wears on tempers, patience and sleep.
Some people get short and sharp in weather like that. Maybe you're one of them. Guru Arjan looked at that burning month and saw something in it: the same heat doesn't land the same way on everyone.

teach.h: THE HEAT BURNS THOSE FAR FROM THE ONE.
teach.b: The Asarh stanza is on ang 134. In paraphrase: in Asarh, the heat scorches those whose Husband Lord isn't near them.

teach.h: HOPE IN MORTALS, WHO ALSO BURN.
teach.b: They've left the One who is the life of the world, and put their hope in mortal people. Caught up in duality, in what is second, they're ruined, and death's noose is around their neck.

teach.h: AS YOU SOW, SO YOU REAP.
teach.b: As they sow, so they reap; what is written comes to pass. A whole life passes like a night: the night slips by, she regrets it, and she leaves without hope.

teach.h: THE LORD'S FEET IN THE HEART.
teach.b: Then the turn: Asarh is pleasant for the one in whose heart the Lord's feet dwell. Same month, same heat. For one person it's a furnace; for another it's bearable, even pleasant.
The difference isn't the weather. It's what's near. Slow down on one line: they put their hope in mortal people.

Guru Arjan isn't saying don't rely on anyone. Sikh life is built on sangat, community. The problem is resting your whole hope on people who are themselves passing, who get tired and short in the heat too.
When everything you lean on is also burning, there's nowhere cool to stand.
The sowing and reaping line is a farmer's knowledge, in a month of waiting for rain: a harvest is the fruit of what was planted, and a life gives back what was sown.
And the cool center stays the same: the Lord's feet dwelling in the heart.
Keep the One near, and the heat changes.

how: On the sangrand of Asarh, gurdwaras that keep the day read the Asarh stanza of Guru Arjan's Barah Maha, as the summer heat waits on the rains.

o: a dry wind that blows in from the desert
the burning month before the rains come
a summer fast kept until the clouds break

games.q: the month of Asarh — tap the pairs.
p: June into July, before the rains
scorches those far from the One
the Lord's feet in the heart

s: the stanza says the heat of Asarh is the same for everyone
it scorches those far from the One and is pleasant for those with the One near.
the stanza uses the image of sowing and reaping
as they sow, so they reap.
Guru Arjan says never rely on other people
the problem is resting your whole hope on mortals instead of the One.

games.q: two people sit through the same burning Asarh afternoon. one is miserable, one is at peace. what does the stanza say makes the difference?
o: the Lord's feet dwell in one's heart.
games.why: Asarh is pleasant for the one in whose heart the Lord's feet dwell. the heat scorches those whose Lord isn't near.

practice: Breathe slowly, imagining cool air on the out-breath, and think of someone running hot right now: stressed, short-tempered, overwhelmed.

Without judging their heat, picture bringing them something cool, a glass of water, a calm word, ten minutes of help, or simply not adding to their pressure. If you pray, you can say Waheguru for them.

wordCard.voice: Asarh. The heat before the rains: it scorches those far from the One, and is pleasant for the one in whose heart the Lord's feet dwell.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: Asarh, the month of peak heat before the monsoon.

carryVoice: Your line: asarh: keep him near. The same heat can land two different ways. See you when the rains come.
